newsitem.title: POLAND: ZYWIEC AND UNIONS AGREE ON JOB CUTS.
newsitem.headline: ZYWIEC AND UNIONS AGREE ON JOB CUTS.

text.p: Polish brewer Zaklady Piwowarskie w Zywcu SA (Zywiec) and trade unions have agreed on the need to cut jobs as a result of recent plant closings and technological change, the firm said in a statement.
The statement late on Friday said the agreement would encompass 145 workers.
Last month Zywiec said it would lay off 145 of its 990 workers following decisions to shut down its brewery in the town of Bielsko-Biala and stop soft-drinks production.
The company has said it shut down the Bielsko-Biala facility because of its poor technical standard and to move production to the firm's modernised facilities at its Zywiec headquarters.

Zywiec decided to stop producing soft drinks from the beginning of 1997 in line with its plan to focus on core beer production after the expiry of its licencing agreement with Pepsi Cola on December 15, 1996.

The Friday statement said the plant closings would cost Zywiec 5.8 million zlotys but that 1.8 million zlotys of the sum had already been accounted for in last year's earnings and four million zlotys in October of this year.
